3. Defendant No.1 (predecessor of the respondents) contested the suit by filing a written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Amud Molla was the owner of the suit land but it was wrongly recorded in the names of Sarabdi and others in elmali. Sarabdi and Dabaru never possessed the land. Amud Molla sold the suit land to Bakhar Molla (father of defendant No.1) on 21.07.1920 by registered kabala in which Gahar Molla (son of Sarabdi Molla) was an attesting witness. During operation of the rent roll the plaintiff unsuccessfully raised objection and as such the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 5. Mr. Zainul Abedin, learned Advocate-on-Record on behalf of the appellants-plaintiffs submitted that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that both the Courts below after considering the entire evidence on record concurrently found that the plaintiffs suit is maintainable but the High Court Division without adverting those findings abruptly held that the suit is barred by Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. He further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that both the Courts below disbelieved the defendant's claim regarding title and possession over the suit land, and those concurrent findings being finding of fact based on material on record are binding upon the High Court Division an& unless those findings are reversed with proper reasoning the High Court Division cannot reverse those findings and believe the defendant's case whimsically. He lastly submitted that the High Court Division erred in Law in failing to consider that both the Courts below found that the plaintiffs were in possession and subsequently they were dispossessed by defendant No.l. Those concurrent findings being findings of fact are binding upon the High Court Division unless those findings are reversed with proper reasoning. 

 9. On the other hand, admitting the suit property to be the property of Amud Molla defendant No.1 stated in his written statement that it was wrongly recorded in the names of Sarabdi Molla and Dabaru Molla in ejmali and they never possessed the land. The defendant claims that Amud Molla sold the suit land to Bakhar Molla father of defendant No.1 on 21.07.1920 by registered kabala in which Gahar Mona son of Sarabdi Molla was a attesting wit-ness and during operation of the rent-roll survey the plaintiffs unsuccessfully raised objection under section 19A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 10. After perusing the materials on record it appears that leave was granted to deter-mine as to (I) whether the suit is barred by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877; (ii) whether the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that both the courts below disbelieved the defendant's claim regarding title and possession over the suit land by giving concurrent findings and the same being finding of fact based on materials on record are binding upon the High Court Division and lastly, OH) whether the High Court Division erred in law in failing to consider that both the courts below found that the plaintiffs were in possession and subsequently they were dispossessed by defendant No.1 and those being concurrent findings of facts are binding upon the High Court Division.
